role: conditional two-call information necessity bound, not a new service obligation or an impossibility claim for the actual 95-call history
registration_context: receipt-forecast pilots and their initial numerical-origin replays observed; first import deficit follows a correct forecast whose corrective PN starts too late. The analytic lower-span argument is proposed; no bound artifact or optimistic pulse-band kernel evaluation has been generated

conditional_support.directions: at a nomination before the first call both import and export remain possible; after either first direction both signs of the second call remain possible. All four active sign pairs are diagnostic support branches, not new observed service samples
conditional_support.clock: first call at an hourly clock, second call 60 minutes later; each pulse ramps for one minute, holds for 30 and returns for one. Thirty-minute PN and a 60-minute nomination lead leave the first return/tail PN fixed before observing the first sign
conditional_support.nonanticipation: the same starting inventory, first ramp reference and return/tail PN must be used for both possible first signs; later PN may depend on the first observed sign
conditional_support.relaxations: for the second pulse permit each unit alone the entire 98 MW gross bound, allow its ramp references to know the second sign, and ignore other-unit coupling, no-activation reference safety and the post-pulse tail. Failure of this optimistic necessary band rules out a uniform two-call guarantee under the stated support
conditional_support.scope: no new permanent bidirectional reserve duty; the actual task still only assesses activated requests

analytic_work.inventory_rate: g(p)=eta_c*max(-p,0)-max(p,0)/eta_d, with decreasing slope magnitude at least kappa=min(eta_c,1/eta_d)
analytic_work.first_call_stock_separation_lower_bound_: B=A*(eta_c+1/eta_d)*(30/60)+2*kappa*A*(1/60). The common reference tail cancels between first-import and first-export outcomes
analytic_work.optimistic_second_band: L=-min_delta for a full export pulse whose start and return reference are both -98 MW; U=C-max_delta for a full import pulse whose start and return reference are both +98 MW. Continuous extrema are required over the 32-minute pulse
analytic_work.certificate: if B>U-L with the original physical tolerance allowed at both stock edges, the two possible first outcomes cannot both lie in the necessary band for serving either second sign
analytic_work.proof_requirement: derive the ramp gap from the inventory-rate slope bound and show the extreme second-pulse references are optimistic by pointwise monotonicity; no controller-policy or probability inference

component_probes.purpose: compare saved-context first-call stock separation with the analytic lower bound and the optimistic second-call stock-band width
component_probes.storage: compact metrics and proof explanation only; no controller rollout or weekly trace

decision: a positive gap establishes only the stated uniform-support impossibility; retain the actual pilot negatives and reassess the task and nomination-time information before another controller change. A nonpositive gap is inconclusive and does not certify feasibility. Do not estimate the original 0.05 chance criterion from this bound
limitations: the bound concerns serving all four possible active sign pairs under a specific information schedule. It does not establish that every causal policy fails on the retained deterministic history, quantify a stochastic failure probability, identify real BM dispatch, or demonstrate OR submission readiness
